what: A row of photos drifts sideways on its own via Splide auto-scroll (.4 px/frame on wide screens, .2 on narrow). Hovering over the strip slows it like braking, by 1% per frame (about 1.1 seconds to half speed), until it stops, and on release it returns to full speed at once from that frame. The counter below shows the current slide number and total slides, the progress line fills as it flows, and the previous and next arrows advance one slide in 1s

options.speed: Speed on wide screens (px/frame), default 0.4 — negative flows to the right (make the two rows opposite each other)
options.brake: Ratio by which each frame slows while hovered, default 0.01 — at 0 hovering does not stop it · at 1 it stops at the frame where the hover lands and resumes its own speed on release (the same pause as Splide pauseOnHover — keyword strip)
options.move: Length of the arrow-driven slide (ms), default 1000
options.clones: Number of cells cloned before and after, default 10 (so the strip never goes empty even with few cells)
options.drag: With free, it stops by inertia where dragged instead of snapping to a slot (Splide drag: "free"), default fits the cell
options.[data-fx-part=count]: Spot for the current slot number (optional)
options.[data-fx-part=bar]: Bar inside the progress line (optional) — give the outer box overflow hidden and it fills as far as it has flowed
options..splide__track · .splide__list · .splide: Splide Frame as is. Slide width follows the photo size (autoWidth)
options..splide__arrows > .splide__arrow--prev ·: Arrow (optional) — does not follow the link even when inside a link wrapping the strip

The progress line also follows the original formula as is (remainder after dividing by 1/3 of the list width, keeping the previous value if it turned back more than half).
